learn.title: How fast is it changing?
learn.body: Slope measures a steady rate. For a curve the rate changes. The average rate of change of $f$ from $x=a$ to $x=b$ is $\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}$. It is the slope of the line through two points on the graph, called a secant line.

learn.title: Average speed of $s(t)=t^2$
learn.body: Distance in meters, time in seconds, from $t=1$ to $t=3$.

learn.title: Units tell the story
learn.body: The rate has units of output per input, such as meters per second or dollars per day. If you write the units, the meaning is clear.

learn.title: Shrinking the interval
steps: The averages get close to 2, a hint of the instant speed at $t=1$.
